lawyer:
Rajat Kurth Chakraborty, Advocate—For the Accused-Appellant. 
Mahfujur Rahman (Likhon), AAG with Mirza Md Soyeb Muhit, AAG with Sayeda Jahida Sultana Ratna, AAG—For the State.
full_judgment: 9. Mr Rajat Kanti Chakraborty, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused-appellant has placed the memo of appeal, FIR, charge-sheet, evidence and judgment of the trial court and submits that the prosecution has been failed to prove the charge against the accused-appellant by adducing any independent and neutral witness. He submits that the order of conviction and sentence is not sustainable in the eye of law in view of the fact that the ingredient of the offence under section 302 of the Penal Code against the accused-appellant has not been proved He submits that the accused-appellant had neither intention nor guilty mind to kill the deceased (his wife) at the time of occurrence and as such without intention to cause death or to cause such bodily injury as cause death which will come within the mischief of section 304 part II of the Penal Code. He submits that occurrence took place on 14-9-2015 and FIR has been lodged after 6 (six) months i.e. on 18-3-2016 but there is no acceptable explanation of such delay. He submits that there is no eye witnesses as found from the evidence of all PWs, more so the learned Sessions Judge arrived at decision on misreading, misconstruing the evidence on record and the provisions of law, only on illegal presumption has came to decision which is liable to be set-aside for the ends of justice. He submits that when the victim was seriously ill immediate after occurrence the appellant has taken his wife (victim) to the Hospital with the collaboration of his father-in-law (Informant) and the deceased has breathe his last on the way to the Noakhali Sadar Hospital the accused-appellant was with her, so it is clearly proved that the accused-appellant had no guilty mind to commit any offence as alleged in the First Information Report and as such the judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set-aside. In support of his contention he has referred decision of a case Ali Hussain alias Ali vs State, reported in 13 BLC 163.
